definitions.explanation: Having no value, worth, or usefulness. Used of objects, ideas, efforts, or a person's self-image when they are judged to be of no worth at all.

examples.japanese: そんな{情報|じょうほう}は{無価値|むかち}だ。
{努力|どりょく}が{無価値|むかち}だとは{思|おも}わない。
examples.english: I don't think the effort was worthless.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}が{続|つづ}くと、{自分|じぶん}を{無価値|むかち}な{人間|にんげん}だと{感|かん}じてしまうことがある。
examples.english: When failures pile up, you can end up feeling like a worthless person.

notes:
Composed of {無|む} (without) + {価値|かち} (value). A na-adjective (and noun) meaning having no value at all. Its opposite is {有意義|ゆういぎ} (meaningful) or simply {価値|かち}がある (to have value).

USAGE:
- As a na-adjective: {無価値|むかち}な + noun ({無価値|むかち}な{物|もの})
- As a predicate: {無価値|むかち}だ / {無価値|むかち}に{感|かん}じる

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無価値|むかち}なもの: a worthless thing
- {無価値|むかち}だと{感|かん}じる: to feel that something is worthless

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無意味|むいみ}: meaningless; pointless — stresses lack of meaning or purpose, not lack of worth
- {価値|かち}がない: to have no value — a phrase with the same sense, more everyday in tone
